dailyTopNewsBrief.headline: Bills Rule Out Key Starter Trio Ahead of Week 11 Divisional Matchup
dailyTopNewsBrief.summary: Buffalo hosts the Miami Dolphins in Week 11 seeking to maintain top AFC seeding despite missing core starters at tight end, cornerback, and linebacker. Head coach Joe Brady's offense must adapt to key absences while defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard relies on aggressive third-down pressure packages.
bullets: Buffalo ruled out starting tight end Dalton Kincaid, cornerback Christian Benford, and linebacker Dorian Williams for Sunday's division clash, per [Joe Buscaglia](https://bsky.app/profile/joebuscaglia.bsky.social/post/3n2w23ctesk2z) and [buffalobills.com](https://www.buffalobills.com/news/buffalo-bills-inactives-vs-dolphins-week-11).

To reinforce depleted unit depth against Miami, GM Brandon Beane elevated veteran linebacker Shaq Thompson and cornerback Tre'Davious White from the practice squad, per [Buffalo Bills Official](https://www.buffalobills.com/team/transactions/#tx-45a428167e90).

Defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard has dialed up pressure significantly, raising third-down blitz rates from 30.9% in Weeks 1–6 to 44.1% in Weeks 8–10 (83.4% on 3rd & 7–10), detailed by [Anthony Prohaska](https://bsky.app/profile/proant.bsky.social/post/3n2vzn5hxis22).

Despite leading the NFL in offensive EPA (+12.28) and red-zone touchdown rate (82.8%), Buffalo remains vulnerable defensively with a 31st-ranked sack rate (4.6%) and 30th-ranked tackle-for-loss average per game (3.78).
